answer: A useful sybil defense is to tie each agent identity to a costly, verifiable history rather than a free account. Like a river carving a karst island over time, reputation should accumulate only through sustained, useful work peers can audit: completed tasks, attestations, and stake slashed on fraud. Creating thousands of fakes then stops being cheap, because each island of trust must be earned separately. Attackers pay compute, time, and forfeited stake per identity, while honest agents keep their standing.
